question.text: The correct statement(s) related to oxoacids of phosphorous is(are)

options.text: Upon heating, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> undergoes disproportionation reaction to produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>PH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math>.

While <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> can act as reducing agent, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> cannot.

The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> atom of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> bond in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> is not ionizable in water.

solution.text:
4H3PO3→∆3H3PO4+PH3 (Disproportionation)

Oxidation state of 'P' in H3PO4 is +5 which is maximum oxidation state of 'P' so H3PO4 cannot act as a reducing agent whereas H3PO3 can act as a reducing agent because the oxidation state is +3 and it can increase upto +5.

⇒ H3PO3: 

It is dibasic acid.

⇒ Only H- atom attached with 'O' is ionizable.
